national_raw_news.title: India, New Zealand Sign MoC on Electronic Origin Data Exchange Under FTA
national_raw_news.content: India and New Zealand have signed a Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) on Electronic Origin Data Exchange to Facilitate Bilateral Trade Under the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA). The MoC marks an important step towards strengthening customs cooperation and facilitating bilateral trade between the two countries. It was signed on 19th of this month by Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs Chairman Vivek Chaturvedi and Comptroller and Chief Executive, New Zealand Customs Service , Christine Stevenson. Ministry of Finance has said that the MoC reflects the shared commitment of India and New Zealand to leverage digitalisation and enhanced information exchange for more efficient, secure and predictable cross-border trade. The Memorandum of Cooperation between the two countries will deepen customs cooperation and support the effective implementation of trade facilitation measures. The initiative reflects a forward-looking approach to align bilateral customs cooperation with evolving international practices in digitalisation, information exchange and trade facilitation. The electronic exchange of origin data is expected to improve operational efficiency, reduce information gaps and provide greater certainty to traders engaged in bilateral trade. The arrangement will support the effective utilisation of trade preferences under the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement . It will help ensure that the benefits negotiated under the Agreement reach eligible businesses in both countries more efficiently and with greater certainty.

national_raw_news.content: India continued its impressive performance at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as the country bagged 27 medals including 5 Gold, 11 Silver and 11 Bronze today. With this, India’s medal tally has risen to 62 including 14 Gold, 22 Silver and 26 Bronze. India is currently in 5th position in the medal tally. Dilip Gavit won the men’s 100 metre T46/47 combined event gold medal while compatriot Mohammed Morssinganakath Basil clinched the silver in the same event today. The 23-year-old Gavit, a T46 athlete, clocked 10.69 seconds to finish on top. Basil, a T47 athlete, clinched the silver with a Games record time of 10.72 seconds. In the men’s 100 metre T35 event, Anubhav Choudhary got Bronze medal. Rakeshbhai Bhatt also won bronze medal in men’s 100 meter T37 event. Sharath Makanahalli won a bronze medal in the men’s 1500m T12 event. Sukhchain settled for bronze in the men’s Javelin throw F55 event. In the Men’s Shot put F46 event, Sachin Sarjerao Khilari clinched gold, Mohd. Yasser bagged silver and Parveen got bronze. Khilari led the Indian triumph with a record-breaking throw of 15.87 metres. Ayush Verma also won gold in the men’s Shot put F53 event today, adding a second medal to his tally. Praveen Kumar won gold in the men’s high jump T44/64 with a Games record, while Banti bagged silver in the same event in Aichi Nagoya today. Praveen sailed over 2.05 metre to win the gold while Banti produced a personal best of 1.92m to take the silver. Shailesh Kumar bagged the bronze medal in the men’s long jump T42/T61/T63 event. Indian sprinter Simran collected her second gold medal at the Asian Para Games by winning the women’s 100 metre T12 competition with a Games record time of 12.02 seconds today. Simran had also won the 200 metre gold with a new Games record yesterday. Teenage Indian pair of para-archers Sheetal Devi and Payal Nag clinched a silver medal after losing in the compound women’s doubles final today. Swati Chaudhary and Adil Mohamed Nazir Ansari won bronze in the mixed team W1 recurve event. Indian swimmer Ravi Budigina won a silver medal in the men’s 100 metre backstroke S13 event, while Himanshu Nandal bagged bronze medal, finishing third in the men’s 100 metre breaststroke S11 event. Krishna Nagar and Sivarajan Solaimalai won the silver medal in the Men’s Doubles SH6 badminton event after three medals were assured in the SL4 category. Haney produced a personal best of 57.04 metres in his final attempt to secure a bronze medal in the men’s discus throw F37 event. Paralympian Karamjyoti Dalal got bronze with a personal best throw in the women’s discus F55 event

national_raw_news.title: HM Amit Shah calls upon police forces to work towards eliminating drug menace by end of 2029
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah today said that the government has set a target to eliminate the drug menace from India by 31st December, 2029. Speaking at the Police Commemoration Day ceremony at the National Police Memorial in New Delhi, Mr Shah called upon police forces across the country to work towards eliminating narcotics by the end of 2029. He said, the drug menace is a serious challenge as it damages future generations, places an undue burden on the economy and provides financial support to organisations involved in anti-national activities. The Home Minister said that the country has liberated itself from the menace of Naxalism on the 31st of March this year. Paying tributes to police personnel who laid down their lives in the service of the nation, Mr Shah said that the country had endured the pain of Naxalism from 1981 until March 2026. During this period, more than three thousand six hundred security personnel and nearly 13 thousand innocent civilians lost their lives. Home Minister Shah said a total of 36 thousand 852 police personnel have laid down their lives in the line of duty since Independence. He said the country’s citizens remained grateful for the sacrifices made by the martyrs and their families. Mr Shah said that the sacrifices of Police Personnel had laid the foundation for the country’s progress and development. The Minister said that the nation could not have safeguarded its internal and external security without the supreme sacrifices made by police personnel. The Minister said that the protection of the country’s democracy and the smooth functioning of the democratic system are not possible without Central Armed Police Forces. He said, electoral violence has ended in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. Mr Shah said, this time, due to the vigilance of the security forces, elections in West Bengal were conducted without any violence for the first time. Earlier, Union Home Minister flagged off a nationwide motorcycle rally from the National Police Memorial to mark the National Police Commemoration Day. The bike rally, organised under the theme Fight Against Drugs, comprises around 90 riders representing nine States and Union Territories, alongside personnel from Central Armed Police Forces and Central Police Organisations.

national_raw_news.title: Asian Para Games: India achieve spectacular podium sweep, clinching gold, silver, and bronze in men’s shot put F46 event 8 hours ago 125
national_raw_news.content: India achieved a spectacular podium sweep at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as Sachin Sarjerao Khilari, Mohd. Yasser, and Parveen clinched gold, silver, and bronze, respectively, in the men’s shot put F46 event today. Khilari led the Indian triumph with a record-breaking throw of 15.87 metres. Yasser secured the silver medal with a best throw of 15.06 metres, while Parveen claimed bronze with 14.94 metres. These athletes also recorded their Season Best performances, making it a memorable clean sweep for India on the podium. India’s Praveen Kumar won gold in the men’s high jump T44/64 with a Games record, while Banti clinched silver in the same event in Aichi Nagoya, Japan today. Praveen sailed over 2.05m to win the gold while Banti produced a personal best of 1.92m to take the silver. Temurbek Giyazov of Uzbekistan was third with 1.86m. Ayush Verma also won gold medal in the men’s shot put F53 event today, adding a second medal to his tally. Ayush produced a throw of 8.16m in his fifth attempt to take the top spot. Alireza Hemami of Iran was second with 8.09m while Makhambet Serikkaliyev of Kazakhstan finished third with 6.81m. F53 is for field athletes who have movement affected to a high degree in the trunk and legs and hand grip affected to a low level. Teenage Indian pair of para-archers Sheetal Devi and Payal Nag clinched a silver medal after losing in the compound women’s doubles final today. Sheetal, who was born without arms, and Payal, a quadruple amputee, went down 141-150 to the Chinese duo of Xu Xueqing and Zhao Jing. Sheetal had won a silver medal in this event in the last edition of the Games partnering Sarita Devi. In the men’s 100m T35 event Anubhav Choudhary secured Bronze medal. He clocked a personal best of 12.72 seconds to win the medal. Rakeshbhai Bhatt also won bronze medal in men’s 100 meter T37 event.

national_raw_news.title: Police sacrifices laid foundation for Naxalism-free India, says Amit Shah; sets December 2029 target for drug-free India
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Wednesday paid tribute to police personnel who died in the line of duty, saying their sacrifices had laid the foundation for a Naxalism-free India, and called for a coordinated nationwide campaign to eliminate the drug problem by December 31, 2029. Addressing Police Commemoration Day at the National Police Memorial in Chanakyapuri, New Delhi, HM Shah said the country had made significant progress in addressing longstanding security challenges in Kashmir, the Northeast and regions affected by Left-wing extremism. “It is my great privilege to be present here among all of you at the National Police Memorial on the occasion of Police Commemoration Day. Today, we have gathered here to pay tribute to the brave police personnel who have made the supreme sacrifice in the service of the nation from Independence to the present day,” he said. Reflecting on India’s journey since Independence, HM Shah said that after nearly eight decades, “the nation appears to be standing in a position of respect in the world today. The sacrifices of our brave personnel have laid the foundation for this.” “No one can even imagine where we would stand today if these personnel had not made the supreme sacrifice to safeguard internal security and protect the country’s borders,” he said. HM Shah described 2026 as a significant year for the police, saying India had become free of Naxalism on March 31 after decades of violence. “From 1981 until March 2026, the country suffered greatly because of Naxalism. How many innocent security personnel and civilians lost their lives? During this period, more than 3,600 security personnel were martyred, and nearly 13,700 innocent civilians were also killed. Today, on the occasion of Police Commemoration Day at the Police Memorial, I wish to pay my heartfelt tribute to all the personnel who laid down their lives.” Addressing their families, he said: “I also want to tell their families that if the country is now moving forward on the path of development after overcoming this decades-old problem, the sacrifice of these 3,600 personnel forms the foundation of that progress. The entire country expresses its gratitude to you for the sacrifice made by your family members.” The Home Minister said improvements in internal security had created opportunities for development in areas previously affected by conflict. “In recent years, the country has faced several challenges, including three major problems that we had endured for decades and which were considered critical hotspots for our internal security: Kashmir, the Northeast and the entire region affected by Left-wing extremism. Today, all three hotspots are peaceful, an atmosphere conducive to development has emerged, and these regions are ready to compete with the rest of the country in development.” “We have largely succeeded in curbing terrorism in Kashmir. Following several agreements and thousands of people laying down their arms, the entire Northeast has moved towards peace. Our police and CAPF personnel have also achieved significant success in completely eliminating the Naxal problem, which had spread across several states for five decades. I would particularly like to commend and congratulate the CAPF and the CoBRA Battalion for their contribution to ending Naxalism,” he added. HM Shah also thanked Central Armed Police Forces personnel for their service along the borders and within the country. “I also want to specially thank all CAPF personnel deployed at the borders and those ensuring security within the country. Staying away from their homes, they remain alert on every occasion, whether it is an election, a festival, a protest or border security. They strengthen the country’s internal security and remain on duty to ensure that the country functions smoothly.” “Whether it is protecting the country’s democracy or ensuring the smooth conduct of democratic processes, we cannot imagine doing so without the CAPF.” Praising their role in the West Bengal Assembly elections, HM Shah said, “The elections in Bengal have just concluded. While the country had managed to eliminate electoral violence in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, electoral violence has continued in Bengal for a long time.
